comment: What the command view needs to know about programs, as data (see audit/shellview.py). A quoted argument or a here-document is data unless the program that receives it runs it. 'shell_tools' maps a host tool to the argument that holds a shell command line; 'shells' run a script given with -c, as an operand or on standard input; 'interpreters' run code given with one of their flags, as an operand or on standard input; 'string_carriers' run the words they are given as a command line (their quoted arguments are read as shell). Extend a list to teach the view a program; a program that is not listed is treated as a data consumer. 'shell_option_arguments' are the shell options that take the next word as their argument (so it is not mistaken for a script operand); 'stdin_carriers' turn what is piped into them into words of a command.
